subject: URGENT: KV "frosting" causing extreme tail latency and 502 storm - decision requested
messages:
From: ops@brightline.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-12T23:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99/502 spike - Brightline production

Marcus / Redwood ops,

We started seeing a sharp jump in tail latency around 22:45 PDT and a flurry of 502s. Traffic volume is within normal bounds (±5%), but p99 jumped from ~420ms to >6s and error rate spiked to 6% for a 15-minute window. Our product team is seeing timeouts and partial responses which are impacting checkout flows.

Attached the logs we collected from our side. We've temporarily throttled user-initiated jobs to reduce customer impact. Can you confirm whether this is a regression on your end or something in our usage pattern?

Sara (CTO) is copied. Please escalate if needed.

- Brightline Ops

Attachments: brightline-logs-09-12.tar.gz (referenced), client-error-sample.json
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: ops@brightline.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-13T01:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99/502 spike - Brightline production

Thanks for the report — I’m pulling thread and metrics now. Initial summary from our first pass:

- Root symptom: short-lived but severe tail-latency and 502s coinciding with heavy prefix-hot churn on the KV store.
- Observed behavior: aggressive batching backlog + indiscriminate prefetching appears to fill KV slots with large prefix sets; when a few hot prefixes rotate, hot keys evict others and cause head-of-line queueing on GPU inference lanes. That manifests as long tail and intermittent 502s when requests exceed slot wait time.

I attached a csv with correlated KV eviction counts and per-lane queue depth from 22:30–23:10. Key evidence: three rapid spikes of eviction_rate -> lane_wait_time -> token-timeout.

Immediate ask: Can Brightline keep throttling non-critical jobs for the next 90 minutes while we test a mitigation? We are going to:
1) Temporarily reduce batch window from 50ms -> 10ms for their tenant (to reduce large queue build-up).
2) Lower automatic prefetch concurrency for their prefix-store to 2 concurrent prefetchers.
3) Warm a reserve lane pool and route ~20% of their traffic to that pool to avoid HOL during exercise.

I’ll apply the changes in a staged way and monitor. If you want us to take traffic off-host entirely (failover to dedicated pool), we’ll need a written escalation/exec approval — that’s the ask to leadership here because it touches capacity billing and SLAs.

Attaching: kv-metrics-20280912.csv, incident-slo-log-09-12.txt

Folks — this is bleeding into account health and Sara (Brightline CTO) is on the thread. I agree with Marcus’s triage. A couple of operational notes and an ask for exec sign-off:

Operational mitigations I can run now (no exec sign-off required):
- Push batch_window -> 10ms for Brightline tenant (test on 10% traffic then 50%).
- Decrease prefix prefetchers to 2 and set per-prefix eviction threshold higher for 30m to avoid instantaneous churn.
- Drip-evict small least-recently-used prefixes rather than coarse-grain flushes.

Actions needing exec approval:
- Failover to Reserved Dedicated pool (estimated cost delta for 24h: $6,200) — avoids HOL entirely for the duration of the incident and buys time for safe long-term config changes.
- Proactive customer credit for service disruption (recommend 10% credit for the billing period).

I’ve drafted a short customer-facing message (below). If leadership approves the Dedicated failover, I’ll coordinate capacity with infra and trigger the migration.

Customer message draft: "We experienced a service degradation affecting some inference requests. We've applied targeted mitigations and are preparing a reserve capacity migration to restore stable latency. We will post a full incident summary within 48 hours."

Please approve or provide alternate guidance.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: playbook-eviction-steps.md (internal runbook)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-14T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99/502 spike - Brightline production

Quick operational update + decision request thread.

What we validated overnight:
- Reducing batch window decreased median queue depth but did not entirely eliminate eviction bursts when hot prefixes rotated.
- Prefetch concurrency reduction reduced the amplitude of eviction spikes.
- Reserve lane routing removed >95% of 502s for routed traffic; uncovered a secondary issue where multi-prefix requests still contend on shared KV slots.

Proposed short plan (24–48h):
1) Immediate: route 25% of traffic to reserve pool (we can do this now).
2) Short-term (next 4h): increase per-tenant reserved-prefix slots by 30% and enable soft-protect for top-500 prefixes observed in the last 24h.
3) Medium-term (48–72h): ship a KV-eviction backoff that spaces prefetch retries (reduces synchronous hot-prefix re-insertion).

Decision needed from leadership: approve Dedicated-failover for 12–24h to restore customer SLA while we push medium-term code fix. This is a hard decision because it triggers billing and capacity commitments. If execs decline, we continue with soft mitigations and escalate the customer credit conversation.

Jonas
Staff SE — Runtime Reliability
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: sara.chen@brightline.com
Date: 2028-09-15T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99/502 spike - Brightline production

Leadership / Execs — putting a clean, time-bound ask in front of you. Summary: Brightline experienced a short but high-impact outage window caused by KV prefix churn interacting poorly with our batching+prefetch policy, which produced HOL blocking and consumer-visible 502s. We have mitigations that reduce customer impact, but the only fully-safe short-term step is a Dedicated-failover for 12–24 hours while we deploy a software-level eviction backoff.

Requested immediate approvals:
- Approve Dedicated failover for Brightline for a 24-hour period to restore SLA (estimated incremental cost $6,200).
- Approve a 10% billing credit for the affected billing period to preserve relationship.
- Authorize the incident escalation note to go to Sara (CTO) and their execs by EOD once we confirm routing.

If approved, operational runbook we will run in order (I will be on the bridge):
1) Notify Brightline ops that we are executing failover and confirm maintenance window (5m heads-up).
2) Route 25% traffic to reserve pool; validate error rate and tail-latency for 15m.
3) If stable, move remainder of traffic to Dedicated pool and mark tenant with elevated eviction-protection flags.
4) Open a postmortem and commit to a medium-term code patch (KV eviction backoff + per-prefix soft-protection).

I recommend we approve — this is the fastest way to stop customer impact and buy engineering time for a durable fix. If leadership prefers not to approve, we proceed with soft mitigations and prepare a longer customer remediation plan (larger credit + extended SLA monitoring).

Marcus Lin
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
